entries.developer_comments:
~ NPC dialogue line
~ Since we're stripping you down to flesh and bone you need to survive, we
can take the time to salvage your CBMs, and keep it all intact, reinstalled
in your new Cyberframe.  But your limbs and other parts will be
exchangeable, like bionics.  In the future, if you take off a limb, you'll
have to remove your CBMs, fix them, clean them, and reinstall them.
identity: Since ye've gotta strip down t'vital flesh n' hard scones, we'll salvage your bright'n'steelies, and repackage them in the new frame.  After, you can swap your wiggles and wobs, that is yer limbs and digits, like steelies, with a bit of effort.  If ye plan to do that, also plan to remove your implants, fix'em, clean'em, and shove'em back in.

identity:
At 1545 yesterday, GRAY DAWN mathematician Sylvia Ho was eating a snack in one of the break areas when Dr. Sanchez-Perez approached her and asked her if he could sit with her.  According to Sanchez-Perez, she nodded and he sat and engaged her in conversation about her day and the course of her training and participation in experiments.  Though seeming slightly distracted, Ho answered Sanchez-Perez's questions and continued as the conversation shifted toward the next Superbowl when she suddenly grabbed her lunch tray in both hands and hit Sanchez-Perez in the head with it with full force, fracturing his cheekbone.  Ho showed no reaction to Sanchez-Perez's signs of distress, continuing to eat her snack without attempting to offer first aid, and made no attempt to flee the scene.

When questioned later, Ho said that Sanchez-Perez was "annoying me" and that she "just wanted him to go away."  When asked why she didn't attempt to disengage from the conversation verbally, she had no response other than a shrug.

Dr. Sanchez-Perez, is convinced that this is a side effect of the PATIENT MOSAIC process and has suggested that Ho be examined by a member of GLASS ANVIL to determine any further undesirable effects.
